sync-with-azure-blob: Two sync backends behind ICloudStore, selected by sync.provider row (default s3). R1: exactly one active provider — sync add <provider> deletes the other's rows BEFORE writing (crash between delete and write leaves sync off, visible, never stale secrets; settings merge LWW would otherwise spread them).
R2: unknown sync.provider values route as s3; sync show prints the RAW row so a typo is diagnosable.

Azure ETag trap: the SDK's ETag struct stores verbatim and Blobs writes IfMatch.ToString() (G format) straight into the If-Match header — must construct new ETag($"\"{etag}\"") quoted. Pull/upload response etags come quoted; store unquoted (Trim('"')) to match S3. Pinned by Push_WithETag_SendsQuotedIfMatchHeader.
AzureBlobCloudStore tests use Azure SDK's public HttpClientTransport + Retry.MaxRetries=0 with a canned HttpMessageHandler — no Azurite, no network, hermetic.
sync.objectKey is SHARED across providers (never blanket-deleted); s3-only rows: endpoint/bucket/region/accessKey/secretKey; azure-only: connectionString/container.

sync-cloud-identity-creds: R3 (owner ruling f:): sync --cli modes take NO token options and expect the user to be logged into az/aws CLI. Azure needs --account (the blob endpoint URI is built from it); s3 uses the plain default chain (no profile option — AWS_PROFILE env selects).

Azure no-login failure type is CredentialUnavailableException (probe 2026-08-05), NOT AuthenticationFailedException — both are mapped to SyncAuthFailedException; catch order: 404 first, then credential/auth types, then RequestFailedException 401/403, then HttpRequestException, then generic RequestFailedException.

AWS SDK v4 resolves the credential chain LAZILY: `new AmazonS3Client(config)` succeeds without credentials; the first call throws AmazonClientException. AmazonServiceException/AmazonClientException are siblings (no catch shadowing).

switch-from-stdio-to-http: Serve semantics: foreground/blocking by design (shell backgrounds: 'ai-raccoon serve > serve.log 2>&1 &'); detached daemon rejected (watchdog already solves the leak; honest URL needs the bound port).

stdout contract: serve owns stdout for the URI line or --mcp-entry JSON only; stderr carries everything else; --mcp-entry with a redirect must split streams (> entry.json 2> serve.log) or the JSON corrupts (R5).

Root launch options (--data-root/--install-scope/--transport) are PRE-VERB by System.CommandLine tree design: 'ai-raccoon serve --data-root X' errors with usage; correct form 'ai-raccoon --data-root X serve'. Consistent with all verbs; documented in help ('must precede the verb').

Attach probe: POST /mcp Accept 'application/json, text/event-stream' + non-JSON body -> recognized iff status in {400,405,406} AND body contains 'jsonrpc' (404 excluded: most common foreign answer). False-positive = another MCP/JSON-RPC server on the port; bounded + diagnosable via EventId 605 provenance. No stronger discriminator without a protocol addition (R15).

Watchdog: activity = ANY /mcp request (initialize/list/ping included) — an actively-connected client is 'in use'; guarantee is 'zero HTTP traffic for 4h', NOT 'no tool calls'. Background passes (extraction/watch/sync) never signal; only McpActivityMiddleware calls NotifyActivity (grep-gated).

integration-maintenance: The promotion queue was running TWO scorer generations at once: 204/288 rows carried v1 scores v3 could not reach, because a propose pass emitted only limit=20 deterministic candidates so rows ranked 21+ were never re-upserted. The default limit=50 review window was 100% v3 rows, which is why the sediment was invisible. Eviction ordered score ASC over the mixed column, so it deleted correctly-scored rows and preserved stale ones. Fix decouples the re-score set from the display limit.

A scope tier with few entries captured every scope=all search: the outer RRF scores by rank position alone, so a 1-entry tier's rank-1 and a 2400-entry tier's rank-1 both score weight/(k+1) and TIE, broken by ThenBy(Path, Ordinal). Max-normalization only inflated the displayed 1.0000 - it was not the cause. Fixed by fusing all contexts once against globally-ordered per-modality lists. Single-context parity exact (nDCG@5 0.674, MRR 0.881, sweep grids byte-identical). No measurement in the repo exercises scope=all with two populated tiers, so cross-context ranking quality still has no ground truth.

OTLP: the 5000+ exceptions and the missing metrics are SEPARATE causes, not one bug. Missing metrics = stdio hosts wire no exporter per ADR-0009's dated owner decision, and all real tool traffic is stdio. No code defect; the real gap was that nothing tested the export path at all.
